messages.author: 995acdc01429b8fa
messages.subject: Average over simulations
parts:
Hello,

Is it possible to average out an object over all MCMC simulations that are after the burning period?

Let's say I calculate a large matrix for each simulation. I don't want to get that matrix for all simulations - it would be too big. But I want to somehow average out all elements of the matrix for the entire run and just get the mean matrix. Is it possible to do within the Stan framework? Thanks!

Cheers,
Denis

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Average over simulations
parts:
On Thursday, December 1, 2016 at 10:13:08 AM UTC-5, Denis Perevalov wrote:
Let's say I calculate a large matrix for each simulation. I don't want to get that matrix for all simulations - it would be too big. But I want to somehow average out all elements of the matrix for the entire run and just get the mean matrix. Is it possible to do within the Stan framework? Thanks!

In RStan that is possible. Either specify pars = "big_matrix" and include = FALSE in the call to stan() or sampling(), which will not return the whole posterior distribution of the big matrix. But get_posterior_mean() will still return the posterior means of everything including the mean of each cell of the big matrix. If you want the overall mean of the big matrix, you could calculate that in generated quantities and get its posterior distribution.

Ben

messages.author: 995acdc01429b8fa
messages.subject: Re: Average over simulations
parts:
Hi Ben,

Beautiful! Thanks a lot!

However, I didn't get the part that you said that I can calculate overall mean in generated quantities. generated quantities is executed once per simulation, right? Did you mean some sort of average value over all entries in the matrix? I do want means of each element of the matrix.

In the perfect world, I'd also want to be able to use a custom summary function where I would calculate some statistics. For example, if I'm interested in means and variances of each element over samples. get_posterior_mean() produces just means. Is that possible here?

Cheers,
Denis

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Average over simulations
parts:
On Thursday, December 1, 2016 at 3:24:28 PM UTC-5, Denis Perevalov wrote:
However, I didn't get the part that you said that I can calculate overall mean in generated quantities. generated quantities is executed once per simulation, right? Did you mean some sort of average value over all entries in the matrix? I do want means of each element of the matrix.
Right. If you did want the posterior distribution of the mean across cells of the matrix, then you could do that in generated quantities. But if it doesn't make sense, then don't worry about it.

In the perfect world, I'd also want to be able to use a custom summary function where I would calculate some statistics. For example, if I'm interested in means and variances of each element over samples. get_posterior_mean() produces just means. Is that possible here?

It doesn't do variances. Ideally, Stan should be accumulating those too but it doesn't.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Average over simulations
parts:
Cool. I didn't know RStan did that.

I'm also curious if you do variances, too. You could
use Welford's algorithm to accumulate the variances the
same way you can use a running average to accumulate the
means.

More custom stats would have to be defined and plugged in
as callbacks unless they're function of means and variances.

- Bob

arithmetic operations per parameter per iteration). We're
already writing back on the constrained scale, so we should
have access to everything we need.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Average over simulations
parts: On Friday, December 2, 2016 at 1:45:24 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:

callback handlers.  Do we add another callback handler from

I would say yes. For PyStan and RStan, we would want to put the means and variances into the returned object. For CmdStan, I guess you just write them to another file.

Do
we allow a way to turn it off in case people don't want it to
save the time and memory (it is a few more multiply-divide
arithmetic operations per parameter per iteration).  We're
already writing back on the constrained scale, so we should
have access to everything we need.

I would just make it mandatory. Whatever time you waste during sampling would be mostly made up for by the time you gain calculating the Rhats at the end.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Average over simulations
parts:
I'm more worried about the purely political issue of
everyone trying to run performance comparisons and it
being very hard to compare apples to apples. It probably
won't be too big a drain.

Maybe what we can do is write a filter for the draws
that stores the ongoing calculations. So instead of
having

draw_callback = foo

you'd have

variance_filter vf(foo);
draw_callback = vf;

where the object vf would intercept the draws as they stream
and calculate. Then it would be available for the interfaces
to use as an object rather than forcing them to write callbacks.

- Bob
